title: Assurance Graph v1
description: WBS-20.04. Per the 1.0.17 roadmap's own edge shape (R7 / WBS-20.04): every externally meaningful claim links CLAIM -> failure mode -> control -> check -> fixture/evidence, plus environment, residual limitation, and last verified revision. This is a VIEW over checks that already ran elsewhere (scripts/assurance_graph.py compose_claim), never a second truth store: every failure_mode.check.verdict here must have been produced by actually calling a real sibling control (scope_audit.py, native_evidence.py, merge_passport.py for the pilot claims), never asserted directly into this record. Only the keyword subset scripts/contract_check.py actually enforces is used here (type, required, properties, enum, const, items, minItems, additionalProperties), matching every other contract schema in this repo so a reader of any of them finds the same account.

schema_version.description: Which shape this record follows, so a reader never has to guess.

claim_id.description: A stable identifier for the externally meaningful claim this graph record covers.

claim_text.description: The claim in plain words, exactly as it would be marketed or stated publicly.

failure_modes.description: At least one: a claim naming zero failure modes has nothing checked against it. Each entry is one CLAIM -> failure_mode -> control -> check branch of the graph.

failure_mode.description: The concrete way the claim could be false in practice.

control.description: The real mechanism in this repo that is supposed to prevent or catch the failure mode.

name.description: What this check actually tests, in plain words.

command_ref.description: Path to the real module/function this check calls (never reimplemented here).

fixture_ref.description: What was fed to the control to exercise the failure mode: a test name, a scenario description, or a path.

evidence_ref.description: Where the raw result of running the check can be found or reproduced.

verdict_reason.description: Why the check reached this verdict, non-empty.

environment.description: Where this check's verdict is known to hold (e.g. this repo's CI shape, a specific simulator, or a stated NO-DATA on physical hardware).

residual_limitation.description: What this check does NOT establish, stated plainly rather than implied. May be an empty string only when there is genuinely none.

verdict.description: The worst-of every failure_mode's check verdict (FAIL beats NO-DATA beats PASS), never computed independently of them.

verdict_reason.description: How the overall verdict was reached from the failure modes above.

last_verified_revision.description: The git revision this record's checks were last actually run against, or the literal NO-DATA when that revision could not be determined.
